misconceptions.believed: That W6's decay was correct, having been tested at some length one session earlier: the curve, both directions, purity, every unusable timestamp. Twelve tests.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Displaying it. Building the character sheet against a realistic profile, a tag measured yesterday on one run was missing from the rows and listed under 'not measured yet'.
misconceptions.corrected_to: as_of computed observations=int(self.observations * force), and for a single observation after half a day that is int(1 x 0.97) = 0. Any tag with exactly one run ceased to exist within twelve hours and reappeared in the list of things the player had never done. Rounding rather than truncating means one run survives to one half-life and then expires, the same schedule everything else follows. W6's table moved by one observation at six weeks; the confidence behaviour it was chosen for is unchanged, and the table in T4 is corrected rather than left quoting the old figure.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: Every decay test used six observations, where truncation costs a fraction of a run and nothing visible happens. The bug lived precisely in the case the tests did not use, and that case is the most common one for a new player -- one run on a tag is where everybody starts. Fourth finding in T4 to come from outside the test suite: a claim propagated unchecked (S029), a failure-mode list (S032), and now a screen. The tests were written by whoever wrote the code, so they inherit its blind spots, and a display is the first consumer with different ones. A number nobody renders is a number nobody has checked, however many assertions surround it.

decisions.decision: One row renderer shared by the character sheet and status --why
alternatives: A renderer per screen, tuned to each
decisions.rationale: Two descriptions of the same numbers can disagree, and the player believes whichever screen they opened. Same argument as D197.

decisions.decision: Decayed observation counts round rather than truncate
alternatives: Floor at 1 while any force remains
decisions.rationale: M55. Truncation deletes a single observation within half a day, which is where every new player's every tag begins. A floor at 1 would make one run immortal.

decisions.decision: Aged-out tags are a third category, listed separately
decisions.rationale: Telling a player their own history did not happen is Q91's mistake, and it was about to be repeated on a second screen.

decisions.decision: Tags nobody has played are counted on the sheet
decisions.rationale: 'What could I be measured on' is a question a character sheet should answer. Listing the names costs one line and makes the map of the game visible.

decisions.decision: The sheet states in words that class and attributes are not combined
alternatives: Rely on them being separate sections
decisions.rationale: Exit criterion 8 is about what a screen presents, and saying it is cheaper than hoping the layout implies it.

friction.description: The criterion-6 test from W8 broke again, for the second time, because its slice of the rendered screen swallowed a new section that legitimately varies with mastery. Both breakages reported a criterion-6 failure that was not one. The boundary is now an explicit list of what may follow the class block, with a comment saying why: a test whose scope is 'everything after this heading' will keep being wrong every time the screen grows.

handoff.state: T4 W1-W9 LANDED. The character sheet shows both layers: the function class from how you write, the attributes from what you scored, each with its evidence and neither combined with the other. Exit criteria 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 verified; 3 verified for the two simulated players who can fail (Q89). 1281 tests green unpinned, 1257 pinned, verify clean on 54 reference runs.
handoff.next_action: T4 W10, abilities that act on a boss fight's HP and repair pool. It is the last piece of new mechanism in T4 and the one with a named hazard: power creep dissolves the boss engine. T3 W6 made a fight cost something and an ability that refills repairs freely hands that back. Criterion 7 is the guard -- every ability has a stated cost, and a fight with a full loadout is still losable -- and the instrument check is exactly that last clause, so a simulated fight that cannot be lost is the thing to build first.

A number nobody renders is a number nobody has checked. M55 lived through twelve decay tests because every one used six observations. Is there a cheap general guard -- a property test over observation counts, a rendering smoke test per model -- or is 'look at it' the only honest answer?
